tess: Quick heads-up: newbringup for Orion-12b on the long-context extractive QA slice. Ran three configs: int8 baseline, int6 (q6_k), and int4 per-channel (selective pchan on embed/attn).

omar: Top-line? cost and quality numbers?

tess: Summary: p@3 = int8 0.715, int6 0.709, int4-pchan 0.701. Recall longform: int8 0.694, int6 0.689, int4 0.678. Median latency: int8 230ms, int6 210ms, int4 200ms. 95th: int8 560ms, int6 600ms, int4 660ms. Token cost est: int8 $0.00054, int6 $0.00044, int4 $0.00033 -> per 1M tokens: int8 ~$540, int6 ~$440, int4 ~$330. Samples ~6k queries.

rachel: Patterns look familiar: int6 gives modest quality hit for decent savings; int4 regresses more on recall and has worse tail. Any config notes?

tess: int4 used per-channel on embeddings + attn only, no outlier correction yet. int6 used block-wise q6_k. KV prefix caching enabled for all runs.

omar: Proposed next steps: 1) quick outlier-correction pass for int4 on top-activations; 2) 24h A/B targeted at priming_tokens > 450 comparing int4-pchan+outlier vs int6; 3) derive a simple hybrid selector to route heavy-priming requests to int6 if needed.

rachel: I'll draft the hybrid selector and the GTN blurb showing unit-econ and rollback thresholds. Suggest rollback if live p@3 drops >0.7% absolute.

perf-bot: perf: kicked off microbench outlier-int4 -> run 3292222250

tess: Action items: omar = run targeted A/B (24h); rachel = GTN short memo with econ table and rollback; tess = run outlier microbench and post logs. We'll reconvene when the microbench finishes (ETA ~6h).

pm: please include latency-tail infra delta in the econ notes; int4 higher 95th may increase infra cost for SLOs.

tess: noted. Keeping this thread as the canonical bring-up log for Orion-12b quant experiments.
